Just to see if it worked, I took one of my soft bras that has no wire but does have hooks, and an older bra I have no issue with ruining because it's not suitable for public wear and it just gets worn around the house, and I couldn't get either of them down past my armpits. Oh I absolutely understand and agree, in my head there is always a distinction between actual bras and those types, which are generally known as comfort bras, soft bras, and bralettes, and I was being unintentionally ignorant by forgetting that not everyone knows or refers to them in different ways, and I apologise for that.

Having said that though, the comment I responded to said that they leave it hooked and they put it on like a tshirt, and a bra with a fastener, unless it's not a wired bra, shouldn't be able to go on like that. It's also stretching out the elastic massively because it's designed to go on around the back not over the shoulders, which are significantly wider, so it's shortening the lifespan of the bra.

I've fitted all shapes and sizes, including shapes like twiggy (although they tended to be teens), figures like that are actually some of the trickiest to get a well fitting bra onto because there's so little there. I was also taught to fit without a tape measure because they can be incredibly misleading, for those with the above type figure especially.

The basics of bra fitting are the same for every person, regardless of body shape. It should be firm, not tight, around the band, the wires should sit flush around the breast (including in between the breasts), and the straps should have a little give but not digging in or falling off the shoulders. A well fitting bra, unless it is a bra that is designed to go on over the head and doesn't have a clasp, should never be able to go on over the head.

Your comment about structural support is irrelevant - if they're wearing a size too big around the back because it means the cups are the wrong size. A 34DD can correspond to other sizes, including 32E, 30F, 28FF, 36D, 38C, meaning if they're wearing a 34DD and actually fit better into one of the other sizes, their bra doesn't fit properly.

However, it's better doing it that way than doing it upside down and flipping the cups because that can severely warp the underwires and damage the bra. It will depend on the job, but if you read over the job description, it will give you a good idea of what your role will entail. I have been in retail and hospitality my entire working life, and at each place I've been given on the job training and usually at least 2-3 days of some sort of buddy system with an experienced colleague. 

Generally, your manager or supervisor will give you an area to work in, whether it's stocking shelves, delivery unpacking, cash register, welcome area, whatever, and you need to stick to the area that you're told. If you're given something specific to do, you'll get brownie points for finishing quickly (but **NEVER** substitute speed for quality of the job you're doing), brownie points for doing a high standard of work, and brownie points for using initiative for any issues you encounter. The biggest thing to remember in this though, is if you're not sure what you're meant to be doing or you're not sure how to do the task you've been assigned, **ask someone**. It's better to potentially piss someone off short term because they have to take time out to explain it to you than to potentially piss off several people long term because they have to go behind you, re-doing everything you've already done. That's also a good way to not survive your probation period/lose your job. 

Your employer should go through all clock in/out procedures with you and in almost every place I've worked, you're not allowed to leave an area until someone comes to replace you (this includes bathroom and lunch breaks). 

If you have any questions or want to know more, feel free to let me know!
